title: The 32 crystallographic point groups: operations, characters, and selection rules
conventions: group order  and tables cover ordinary single-valued  point group  only, excluding spin  double group  and  magnetic point group .
Γ labels use standard BC Γ-point labels of representative symmorphic space groups; Mulliken labels are aliases on the same row.

Complex irreducible representations are shown on separate rows. Conjugate rows with Frobenius–Schur indicator 0 must be paired to form real physical representations; each row must not be mistaken for a two-dimensional representation.

IR types are those present in  polar vector  (x, y, z). Raman types occur in the symmetric rank-two tensor under the nonresonant  electric dipole  approximation. This does not guarantee a corresponding vibration or nonzero intensity in a given material.
basis gives a basis of the corresponding isotypic subspace. When multiplicity exceeds 1, it does not claim that each listed function belongs to a different copy.
Basis functions use the active-operation convention f(r) → f(R⁻¹r). Axial vectors acquire an additional det(R), so labels for complex functions x±iy follow this operation convention.
Orthogonal axes follow BC, without forcing the textbook monoclinic b-axis convention. Operation matrices and basis functions use the same coordinates.

validation.method: Exact BC source tables are matched row by row to independent numerical regular representations. Checks cover group closure, character orthogonality, the sum of squared dimensions, polar/axial vectors, and symmetric-square decompositions.
